messages:
alex: Hey support — after we pinned the embeddings model for cust-482 (model pinned to redwood-emb-alpha@v2.1.0 last night) their /embeddings responses are now 1024-d vectors, previously 768. Request id: req_8f3a. Search similarity dropped.
maria: ugh, that's bad. Can you paste a sample response and the model identifier you used in the API call? :eyes:
alex: here's the minimal repro curl we gave the customer:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-alpha@v2.1.0","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.0012,0.0023,...,0.9999],"model":"redwood-emb-alpha@v2.1.0","usage":{}}
```
Length observed: 1024 floats (counted on customer side). We expected 768.
jen: did they pin to a variant that actually maps to a different upstream model under the hood? sometimes our routing substitutes a compat variant if quantization/profile mismatch occurs.
maria: alex — can you share the exact request_id header the customer saw? we need the server logs. also, which region are they hitting?
alex: request-id header returned: r-202103-8f3a. Region: us-west-2.
jen: @tyler any recent routing changes around pinned variants or fallback rules that could swap to a 1024-d model when sequence/quant config mismatches?
tyler: deploy-bot shows a canary rollout for emb-alpha v2.1.0 yesterday at 23:12 UTC with an emergency fallback mapping added (fallback-> redwood-emb-compat-1024) for high-latency nodes. Might be related. I'm checking routing logs for r-202103-8f3a.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary redwood-emb-alpha@v2.1.0 -> traffic 10% at 2024-11-18T23:12:04Z. fallback mapping: emb-alpha@v2.1.0 -> redwood-emb-compat-1024 on node-group gpu-pool-3 when kernel mismatch detected.
maria: if fallback mapping existed, pinned semantics should avoid substitution. Did the pin take effect in the private control plane or only on the routing layer? alex, did you use the pinned API param or did customer pin via console?
alex: customer used the API param pin=true on the model request (we documented). They thought that locked model to v2.1.0. Console shows pinned version active for their account.
jen: potential hypothesis: the pin was applied to the control plane but an autoscaler moved traffic to gpu-pool-3 where the runtime couldn't load v2.1.0 (quant kernel missing) and routing applied fallback despite pin due to a bug in the enforcement logic. tyler can we confirm enforcement behavior?
tyler: confirming logs: for r-202103-8f3a we see a node rejection: "model binary missing: v2.1.0.quant" then router applied fallback variant. Router incorrectly treated pinned flag as soft preference instead of hard lock in that path. filing bug.
maria: mitigation: 1) temporarily unpin and repin to force scheduling on compatible nodes OR 2) pin to explicit variant hash that maps to 768-d model. Which is faster for the customer?
alex: customer wants fast fix. They can accept a hotfix or temporary rollback.
tyler: fastest: roll back routing fallback rule for that account or force-schedule job to compatible node. I'll push a hotfix to treat pinned=true as hard in router for in-flight requests. ETA ~30m to patch and restart router shard for us-west-2.
jen: also add a diagnostic we can surface to customers: returned model name in response vs expected pinned name mismatch. That would have caught this earlier.
maria: alex — tell customer we have a patch in progress. ask them to re-run the same request after 45m and paste the request-id if they still see 1024.
alex: will do. thanks. I'll flag cust-482 support ticket and note rollback option if they prefer it now.
tyler: patch deployed to router-us-west-2 (canary) at +18m, monitoring.
deploy-bot: alert: router-us-west-2 canary patch deployed at 2024-11-19T00:05:10Z.
alex: customer re-tested: request r-202103-9bfc shows embedding length 768 now. They confirmed baseline similarity restored. :relieved:
maria: great. followups: 1) postmortem with timeline and bugfix, 2) add automated check that embeddings length matches pinned model signature, 3) notify billing/priv infra about node binary drift.
jen: adding eval to prevent model-shape regressions during canary->ga. also will add a quick script to map pinned model -> expected vector length in console UI.
alex: thanks all, closing the support loop. :thumbsup:
